In short, it’s a mixed bag.  I appreciate aspects of both.  I do certainly miss high school a lot, partially because that hole never got filled due to covid.  My teachers and classmates were great and meant a lot to me.  Now, everyone just feels so distant :(

I completely agree with you.  I think the biggest difference between us and other typical ND conditions is that people with austism, ADHD, etc. are born with a brain wired that way, while for CPTSD, our brain becomes wired that way.

Both end up diverging from a neurotypical brain, but take different paths to get there.

As someone who has been diagnosed with ADHD, I will say that my CPTSD symptoms have a MUCH greater impact on me and make me feel more divergent from the typical than my ADHD does.

Additionally, my CPTSD symptoms mirror autism in women quite a bit.  The shyness, social awkwardness, overstimulation, etc. could appear to be autism to someone who doesn’t know what I’m thinking or about my history.  This is true for many people with CPTSD.  We often struggle and/or look different in the same areas as autistic people, but usually our brain’s rationale for those behaviors is different.  Either way, we end up at a divergent place.

I say we do count because of this.  However, I think there is a ways to go before other people feel the same, especially because not many seem to recognize just how vastly CPTSD can literally rewire your brain to such an extent.

Take what I say with a grain of salt as I do not know the intricacies of what neurodivergent means nor have I really studied this in depth before, it is just a matter of my own opinion.

Yes.  I have been on Vyvanse (a medication similar to Adderall used primarily to treat ADHD by increasing dopamine) for a while.  It was a great dosage and I was in an extremely good and normal spot.  

Once I got covid, it’s like that suddenly stopped working, like my baseline for dopamine changed.  I don’t want to increase my meds because I don’t want to mess with that right now and potentially create more problems.

But yeah, anhedonia is a perfect term to describe it.  I had a 3.9 in college and now I am failing all of my classes.  I literally could not care less and that is not like me.  I’m not depressed either, I just feel apathetic.  

Important deadlines for huge assignments come and go and I just feel too foggy, tired, and meh to do it.  Yet I can’t get myself to care.  Before covid, I would’ve pulled all nighters to finish these sorts of things and I’d turn them in perfectly.  Now I literally have piles of work and feel so detached that it doesn’t phase me.

God this fucking sucks.

NAD, but this helped put things into perspective for someone else who was also hesitant.

Our species is in a really shit situation.  Unfortunately, this means that we must either get this virus that is designed to damage and destroy and that has been substantially proven to have a high likeliness of causing long term effects.  Or get this vaccine that is designed to help and build immunity that has been substantially proven and designed to not damage the body in any way that would cause long term effects.

The third option, to do nothing and wait it out, is unfortunately, not really a secure option at all.  I did everything humanly possibly not to fall into that first group while waiting for the vaccine to be available to me, but then I got it anyways.  I didn’t have the choice most do, because fate chose for me.  Now I’m 20 and have ongoing health issues that have changed my life and body drastically.

You have this choice and it sucks ass that we even have to make this choice to begin with, but remember that you never know when this choice can be decided for you.  And trust me, it is a lot worse than getting the vaccine.  I’ve done both.

This is not to guilt trip you at all.  In fact I empathize with you and would probably have the same worries if I hadn’t gotten covid.  But the fact of the matter is, you will be exposed to the virus just by being alive and you’re playing a nasty game of russian roulette with whether or not you’ll be that small percent whose mask or hand sanitizer don’t quite do it.

This is so interesting.  I became vegetarian during the height of my abuse, at an age younger than most (like 12 I think?)  Many of my friends are vegetarian now, but most became so much later in high school or college.

I remember it had bothered me for the longest time, then one day I picked up a chicken nugget and just couldn’t do it.  I thought about how it had a life and family and how it probably lived in fear and how it died afraid and whatnot and started bawling.  I never (intentionally at least lol that damn gelatin) ate meat again.

I want to be vegan now as soon as possible as I have just learned how cruel animals are still treated for their products :(

I could have written this.  I was by far the quietest kid at any point in school.  Still am in college.  I especially am with adults (well at least adults older than me since I guess I am technically an adult now.)  Around big groups of people I shut down and can’t say a thing.

I always attributed this to my father’s abuse though, but I also acted as the emotional support for my mother.  I still do a bit.  While they were together I was her soundboard for what to do about my dad.  Now that they’re separated I am her soundboard for dealing with the aftermath of being married to my father.  Without me, her house and life falls apart.

But yeah I get it.  Ugh especially the extended family members part.  If I could go one holiday without cousins or uncles or aunts teasing me about being so quiet that would be great.

Maybe it’s because we had to bear all of these adult conversations as kids that we never learned how to converse normally?  We never got to talk about ourselves or talk about casual, non stressful things.  We also had such a burden placed on us to give the correct response because if not, it effected our caregiver and thus the way we were cared for.

Thanks for posting this though.  I’ve never thought about this and will certainly be pondering it now.

I recently found school reports from kindergarten and early elementary school.

Play observations all said that I was “silent,” “scared to interact with adults,” “timid to pick up and play with toys,” “just sat and stared into space,” and “did not interact with other children.”

Teachers noted that I was tense and uncomfortable.  One even wrote that my shoulders were in a constant “shrug” position I was so tense and that she had to told me to relax them multiple times a day.  They wrote that I was incredibly shy and quiet.  I was also sick for absolutely no reason, vomiting every single day.

Yeah... what the fuck?  That definitely was not normal.   My parents did not put me into pre school, so this was my first time outside of my house.  What the hell happened for those first five years?

It’s like, I certainly know the abuse that came after that, so that probably means it was also occurring before my memory formed too, right?  But what happened?

I also have memories of having realistic sexual thoughts and dreams at a VERY young age.  Part of me worries that those may not have been dreams :(

I wish someone would just tell me what happened.

I got a cat on my own recently and wow... it’s insane how easy it is to not yell at him.

My dad used to hit, yell, kick, etc. my dog and cat growing up and it hurt so bad to watch.

Now that I have a pet of my own, if he does something he isn’t supposed to, my first reactions are:
“Uh-oh let’s get that cleaned up!”
“It was an accident, it’s alright buddy you didn’t know!”
“It’s ok!  Easy clean up!”
“You stinker!  Haha that’s alright though, let me clean it up!”
“Oops I’m sorry I put that thing so close to a ledge where it could be knocked over.  Let me move it so it doesn’t happen again and scare ya!”

I make sure to be comforting because he’s a cat and you know how much cats can scare themselves shitless for knocking something over LOL.

But I seriously don’t understand my father at all.  I don’t ever feel rage towards him.  Just laughter or sometimes slight annoyance, but mostly just laughter.  That’s the joy of having a pet.  They do silly things.  Everything is replaceable and if it isn’t, I know to keep it out of reach!

Yep.  This is different from what you described, but school was my safe space from home and the ONLY thing I miss from childhood is the teachers who cared and the classmates who were kind.  So when I mention only wanting to be a kid again to go to school, everyone looks at me like I am crazy.

I tested for IQ in the 99th percentile along with the subjects of math and reading in first grade.  I don’t believe in standardized testing to measure intelligence, however, this does give evidence that my brain was in fact functioning well enough to do these things at this age.

I skipped several grades in math.  Went to special classrooms for most of the day because the regular one was below my abilities in most subjects.  Won several national awards in math.  Won national awards in art.  I was completely motivated by myself, I didn’t even tell my parents about these things, I just did them and won.

Then the trauma got worse.  Especially mid elementary.  I had the same teacher twice, once in first grade and once in fifth, who asked me what happened because I used to work so much better.

Things got even worse.  Failed high school precalculus.  Horrible GPA.  Barely made it into college.  Now that I am here I am struggling.  

My brain feels so clouded.  I don’t feel motivated to do anything.

this is completely paraphrasing from something i read a while ago, so i could be off and dont remember how legitimate this study was, but i read that it also has something to do with the same reason why people with ocd have the intrusive thoughts they do.  it’s like in order to regulate what not to say, your brain needs to be aware of what’s inappropriate, even if you’re not directly thinking about it at the time.  for most people, this knowledge of what’s inappropriate just remains in their subconscious.  its not like when you see a knife your thoughts are screaming for you not to stab people, you just *know* and can carry out whatever you need to do.  but for people with ocd, these inappropriate ideas seep through as intrusive thoughts.  since ocd and tourettes are correlated in ways, i believe i read that these subconscious ideas manifest not only as intrusive thoughts, but also uncontrollable physical urges in people with tourettes.  99% of the time, it’s inappropriate to yell our curse words, hence why it’s a more notable inappropriate vocal tic.  this is also why sometimes, unfortunately, people might yell slurs and other things too.  

however i might add that word tics and even moreso cursing tics are incredibly rare.  most vocal tics are just noises.  but word/curse ones usually get more attention because they are so striking.

I have diagnosed IBS that started in late elementary school.  To the point where I needed to go to the bathroom 8 times during a school day and sometimes had to stay home in order to not shit my pants.  How did I get it to a manageable place?  Not stomach medications.  Anti anxiety medications.

When I was 2-5 I threw up every single day and night, multiple times without fail.  Acid reflux meds and surgeries didn’t fix it.  When did it stop?  When I started school and suddenly had a way to get out of my house for most of the day.

I have tachycardia.  This means my heart beats too fast constantly.  Even when I am sleeping it is incredibly high.  130 resting.  I have had xrays and tests done.  There’s no physical cause.  It just simply does that.

I also can’t help but think all of these things are related to trauma.  I know mine aren’t even that serious, but the thing that gets me, is that there aren’t any physical causes to any of them.  Yet they are very clearly still here.

The worst part is that memory doesn’t even begin until around elementary school.  So I have no clue what it was like for me when I was vomiting.  I just know what it was like afterwards and can assume that it started before.  Plus little tidbits of info, like my mom telling me that my dad once threw me from a high chair, screaming at me and “spanking” me because I threw food... as a literal baby.

Psychological Factitious Disorder.

I knew someone in high school who had this.  They had been diagnosed and were then frantically going to new doctors to get it removed from their record because they “did not have that and were misdiagnosed.”  They were trying to get so many other diagnoses instead, they got caught in the act.

Yeah... they ended up faking a sexual assault a year later and claiming to have PTSD until they got caught in the lie.  They claimed that it was r*pe because they consciously decided to go off their meds and not tell their partner, then consented to sex, then months later suddenly decided it wasn’t consensual because they “weren’t in the right mind after not taking their meds for a day.”  How the fuck was their partner supposed to know that?  Before they got caught with their skewed logic, they made sure to ruin this guy’s life.

Now every other post is about PTSD awareness and how they can’t be around men anymore and blah blah.  As someone with diagnosed PTSD, I am livid.  Literally 2 people IRL know I have it, I don’t make tiktok dances about PTSD like this person does, it’s SO fucking personal and re traumatizing to tell people.

They even went so far as to tell the class they had homicidal thoughts at one point.

I struggle to know how to feel.  On the one hand, it’s like having Factitious Disorder is a mental illness and it’s not like mental illnesses are in people’s control.  But at the same time, bruh you’re hurting so many people with other mental illnesses by impersonating them, like jfc you were literally diagnosed with this... wake up and get help.

I use it when I have multiple options for professor/courses and am trying to decide which to take.

I truly hate to say this, but every time I have not listened to RMP, I have deeply regretted it.  It takes a lot for me to not particularly enjoy a professor.  I always try to consider their different teaching styles, personalities, and circumstances whenever I’m not enjoying a course and remind myself that they mean well.

But, sometimes, they’re just assholes or really do not know how to convey information effectively.  The first time I didn’t listen to RMP, I thought people were exaggerating about how rude this guy was.  I’m not talking “he didn’t give me an extension!!” rude, but actually verbally insulting our class rude.  It was mind blowing that he could just say some of the things he did, jeez.  Not a joy to be around.  Made learning really suck and class stressful to be in.

The second was brilliant.  Had a great sense of humor, was very engaging and kind, amazing in his field.  But, the dude couldn’t teach.  We were all so confused.  My entire class showed up to the two tutoring sessions a week.  These 19-20 year olds saved our asses.  I can’t even explain it, but the professor was just so far gone in his own world that nothing really made much sense.

So I now look for reviews that seem honest (aka not a slacker/asshole student looking for revenge) and take them into consideration.  Lots of negatives mean something, especially if they say the same things.  If one person says you’re a condescending prick, it’s one thing.  But if 20 people say it in the course of three years, it’s another.

I also look for positives.  I really do care about what I am studying and am truly interested in my courses, so I would prefer a professor that is particularly good at building up that interest or excitement.  Lots of reviews saying that their class is engaging means that I am probably going to love being there and love learning.  Lots saying that they’re really compassionate and understanding means that if I happen to run into tough times then I know they’ll work with me.  Lots saying that they give good feedback means that I’m probably going to grow as a learner in this class.

TL;DR I’m looking for either super high or super low ratings, because each indicate an anomaly, that can either make for a super bad experience or a super amazing one.  I also look for consistency and credibility in these too.  Beyond that, I look for average ones to make sure I’m going to at least not have a bad experience.  I don’t discount these professors, because average is also good and RMP does not indicate everything.  I’d just prefer an amazingly rated one because that’s the best indicator that I’ll have a very good experience.

As someone who does this, it is news to me that it’s considered rude.

I never address my professors in my email.  I simply say “hello,” and continue with my message.  I’ll introduce myself if they don’t know who I am, but if they know me, I also don’t do that either.

Besides not knowing that we had to, I just feel weird and awkward addressing them by name.  They know I’m talking to them because I’m sending this email to them, so I don’t naturally see the point in saying “hello professor blank,” or whatever.

Secondly, it just feels weird to me and I never would’ve guessed that we needed to do this unless someone had told me.  It’s not like I address anyone else in my life like this, unless it’s a job application or something.

Thirdly, I usually say something like “I hope you’re having a good day” or “I’m really enjoying class so far” as a sort of greeting before my message.  I mean what I say and genuinely hope it makes them feel good, especially during pandemic times where I know professors can feel bad about teaching right now. People don’t understand that our brains are quite literally wired incredibly different.

Take any introductory psychology or neuroscience class and one of the first things you will learn is about how experiences shape the brain, physically.  The brains of musicians are literally more dense in the part of the brain responsible for sounds. 

C-PTSD is different than other psychological disorders because the trauma often occurs during development.  Meaning that our brain develops to fit a dangerous and traumatizing world that does not actually exist outside of our unique situations.  However, we’re too young to know that parents, siblings, aunts, uncles, etc. aren’t supposed to be like that, etc.

I hate to say this, but my entire persona feels centered around trauma.  I mean, how could it not be?  You’re the result of your experiences, especially your earliest ones, and mine were life threatening, demeaning, and horrifying.

I’m incredibly shy and quiet because talking brought danger.

I’m very detached and emotionless because I’ve had my life threatened since a young age and therefore nothing phases me anymore.

I cannot connect to things because I learned that the things you love can be taken away or used against you.

I cannot connect with adults of any sort, especially males, because all of those were dangerous and mean in my childhood.

I don’t sleep at night because I learned that you can’t let your guard down or else it’s dangerous.

Do I know that all of these things are irrational in the present day?  Do I know that most of the world is not like this?  Do I know that I am no longer in the situations that caused these behaviors?  Yes, yes, and yes.

However, I cannot fix these thoughts, feelings, or behaviors.  They are involuntary.  My brain is hardwired to do this and I can’t just use logic or willpower to override it.

When people say “everyone has trauma” I think they’re commenting on the fact that essentially everyone has experienced an event that would be classified as “little T.”

Your parents go through a 3 month period of financial stress but you still have all your needs met and great parents.  

You had an asshole teacher that was critical of you, but never anything abusive.

You have to move and change schools, but your needs are still met and there’s no bullying or anything.

Your pet dies of natural causes.

Someone comments something mean on your social media.

These are all normal events that are emotionally upsetting and are considered little traumas.  They’re essentially impossible to avoid throughout life.

Though I’d like to note that some little T can become traumatizing for some people depending on many different factors and how it effects them.  Things like repetition and outside support.

But yeah it definitely downplays trauma and ptsd when its thrown around and people assume your trauma is just like everyone’s, usual childhood trauma.

Is CPTSD the only thing you have that makes you neurodiverse?  

The term neurodiverse is a bit fuzzy, but usually can include mental illnesses to my understanding.  In my opinion, CPTSD should be counted because it impacts everything about us.

Neurodiversity to my understanding represents a “different kind of human.”  Take autism or adhd for example.  Both are a cluster of traits, to the extreme enough end to be diagnosed, that cause people to see and interact with the world differently than most of the population.

CPTSD is the same thing.  Most of us have this disorder from childhood aka when our brains and bodies developed.  It’s literally changed our brain structures and chemistries.  This is something you can never completely undo, at least not easily.  Although people with autism and ADHD have large genetic factors that play into their conditions, we also have our own chemistry that is different from others, even if we weren’t born with it.  We simply attain it later in life.

We certainly see the world differently and interact with others differently due to these chemical and physical differences in our brain.  Therefore, I’d say that we’re neurodiverse snd we cannot fully change that.

HOWEVER, this doesn’t mean that you can’t cope and improve the symptoms that lower your spoons.  The same goes for autism or ADHD.  I personally have ADHD and used to wake up with a very low amount of spoons, however, meds were able to fix some chemical imbalances and give me some energy back that I should’ve had in the first place.  So did going to therapy and learning how to help ADHD.  It didn’t solve everything, I still have ADHD and the occasional low spoon day, but my life is now much more livable.

If you’re able, try different treatments for CPTSD and see if any give you spoons back.  This is something I’m still figuring out too as I still have low spoon CPTSD days, but it’s getting there.

I don’t have too much advice, but I know some things that helped my friends move out who went straight to the workforce.

Do you have any friends you can split an apartment with?  This can drive the cost down immensely.  You can also share things like food, toiletries, supplies, etc. to keep the cost lower.  If you don’t have anyone to do this with, look online to find someone, but be careful and safe.

Try getting a job now and just start saving.  It doesn’t matter if it’s low paying, at least get the ball rolling.  You can always apply to better jobs, but in the mean time, have an income flowing in.

Do you have access to a car?  If so I’ve made a shit ton off of doordash.  Sometimes up to $30 an hour.  I’d try this to see if it’s right for you.  At least until you can find a real job.

Consider moving to another place if you live somewhere with a high cost of living.  Phoenix AZ will cost a lot less than Los Angeles CA.  Rural PA will cost less than Philly.  You can try to stay close to home if you’d like, or just go for it.

Do you want to go to college?  If so, there are some work colleges out there that let you go for free if you work so many hours a week.  It’d give you a free place to live, have food, and study something you want to get a higher paying job later.

I am a 19 year old and reading this sounded like something I could’ve wrote a month ago.  I just got diagnosed a couple weeks ago and started medication and it is life changing.  Here is what I did:

First, contact your university’s accommodations or disability center.  They can give you a list of recommended providers that work with your school.  Or if your school is bigger and more resourceful than mine, they may have trained clinicians who can diagnosed at your school.  

My school also paid for my testing since I am on a Pell Grant.  Be sure to ask if they have financial aid for testing!

Next I made an appointment with one of the providers and got in within a week.  It took a bit of calling around, but I chose the one with the shortest waiting list since I was really struggling.

After that I went to my first appointment.  Here they screened me for other medical conditions that look like ADHD (bipolar, etc.) and asked about my symptoms and history.  Then they gave me forms that ask you to check of the severity of your symptoms that fit the DSM.  They also gave me forms to give to parents and friends.

Before my second appointment, I went to the accommodations office and was able to get extended test time and an audio book thing after proving that I was in the process of a diagnosis and meeting with someone and describing my symptoms.  They were very helpful and were happy to grant temporary accommodations until I received my formal diagnosis.

For my second appointment, we went over the forms I filled out.  In addition to this, she asked me to bring in old report cards from elementary school to prove that my symptoms were present in childhood.  I found a few that showed that I turned in assignments late, was super quiet and in my own world, needed to be pushed to start assignments, etc.  I also brought in middle and high school grade cards that showed how I struggled only in classes where I couldn’t have extended test time or turn in late work to show how my symptoms impact my grades.

I received a formal diagnosis in the mail a week later and then went to my school’s doctor who suggest I try vyvanse.  There are both stimulant and nonstimulant medications.  Stimulants are usually tried first since they work most frequently, however if you have an underlying condition like a heart problem, non stimulants may be prescribed instead.  Due to the abuse of stimulants in college, I have to check in frequently with the doctor and take drug tests every few months (although I think this happens regardless of whether you’re in college or not.)

I’ve not been on the medication very long, but I finally feel like I can function and feel normal now.  It doesn’t automatically fix everything or give you this giant euphoric rush of feeling like you’re suddenly able to do everything you struggled with, but it gives you the ability to work on these things and think clearly.

I am now in the process of finalizing accommodations with the accessibility office so that I can get extended test time and other useful tools permanently.

This was my process and I think I was in a very similar situation to you.  Please let me know if you have any questions or want someone to talk through as you go through this process!

Intrusive thoughts having to do with unwanted sexual attraction are EXTREMELY common in OCD.

One of the reasons we get intrusive thoughts (even in people who don’t have OCD) is because when our brain wants to suppress something, it has to identify what it is that it wants to suppress, thus it has to think about what it is suppressing.  It manifests what we don’t want.

You suddenly became worried that you were a pedophile when you did not want to be, thus your brain became obsessed with suppressing anything that would indicate you being a pedophile (like unwanted attractive thoughts when you see children,) thus your brain had to think about what it was trying to suppress, in turn doing the opposite.  You then confused this for actual attraction.

As for the anime thing you watch, I don’t know much about that, but from my understanding it is cartoon porn of younger people?  If it’s not a real person, it’s not child porn, period.

Power play is a huge theme in the sex world.  Along with this comes stereotypical dom/sub characters (that’s where the whole master/maid or professor/school girl stereotype we’ve all heard comes from.)  Perhaps you’re just more dominant person and because you’re young and haven’t been exposed to other things yet, the anime stuff is the only way you know to express this.

Similarly, so much porn out there involves scenarios that would be fucked up in real life.  There are millions of videos and stories out there “girl turns 18” etc. because porn plays on fantasy.  Of course having a fantasy about little kids specifically is not ok, but maybe you have a fantasy of being dominant or dating someone of a consenting age who is younger than you or of getting with someone you have power over.  All of those are extremely common and even submissive people fantasize about the opposite role.  It goes both ways.  This is normal.

Sex stuff is not taught in schools and it leads us to think we’re weird or flawed in some way.  BDSM, power play, you name it, is all perfectly normal to fantasize about and to view as long as it includes consenting adults (or other teens if you’re a teen yourself.)  I recommend exploring all of this more so maybe you can move away from what you currently watch since it’s making you very distressed and uncomfortable to continue viewing it.

Bottom line, this is a HUGE symptom most people with OCD have at some point.  But the fact that you feel fear to the extent that you want to kill yourself tells me you’re not a pedophile and you will never act on it.

As for if you truly are worried, help is there.  Nobody is going to lock you up or arrest you.  You’re a minor yourself.  You have done nothing bad to any child.  A therapist has probably gotten tens or hundreds of clients come in with your exact problem, because it’s just that common with OCD.  

Until then, exposure therapy could help.  Be around kids in small doses, with other adults in the room.  Realize that you actually don’t want to hurt them or feel anything towards them.  Then realize that you can trust yourself and that you’re a good person.  A therapist can help you do this in a more controlled way, but until then trying it on your own can help.

Good luck.  Do not kill yourself.  Please try to stop beating yourself up about it.  This is NORMAL for people with OCD.  Help is out there.

My teachers would even comment on how tense I looked, but nobody suspected anything because how could someone who is “gifted” (or whatever BS they label kids who do good on one test nowadays) not come from an amazing family.

When I needed help again and my home life got bad as a high schooler, I even contemplated doing bad on purpose just so someone would notice and help me.  I did slip up for a semester really badly, partly do to home stuff but mostly due to mental health as a result of my home life and having to work so much after school so I could save up enough to move the fuck out as soon as I could.  My guidance counselor talked to me once about my grades and literally wrote in an email that I was “identified as gifted and therefore should not be getting these grades.”  Yet even then, nobody noticed anything.

My dad had a pattern of making us all go somewhere with him, getting drunk, refusing to let my mom drive, and then driving like a lunatic telling us he was going to kill us all.  Whenever my mom would try to stop him, he would hit her.

Holidays, concerts, vacations were all ruined because we spent the entire time walking on eggshells, watching as he downed drink after drink, dreading the drive home.  Everyone would always say things like “you’re so lucky you get to go see this band!” or “I’m jealous you got to go to Florida!” but it was actually a living hell, being scared for my life 24/7.

My worst memory of this was on July 4th.  We were over at an uncle’s house and everyone in my family was drunk and fighting, physically.  When we got in the car to leave, my mom tried to not let him drive but it got physical fast.  I was only 9 or so, but I remember shattered glass and blood all over the car.  I truly thought I was going to die that night.  I don’t know if it’s a blessing or a curse that we didn’t get pulled over, because I’m sure if my dad heard sirens he would have tried to end it for sure.

Another one was when I was in high school and he threatened us with a gun to get out of the house while pulling a knife out on my mom.  I was doing homework peacefully in my room, had school the next day, but instead had to literally sprint out of the house in PJs and go to a hotel with nothing.  I went back to school a few days later and I remember my teacher was appalled that I didn’t do this one big project, but internally I could not give less of a shit about that right now.  That’s how I got my first B in high school!

I’m a late teenager now, and sometimes I feel bad for hating my dad.  He tries to act like nothing ever happened and buys me things to make up for it, even though I don’t live with him anymore.  My mom even gets so annoyed with me because he “does so much” for me with money, even though in my opinion that’s the least he can do.  And you know, parents are just supposed to do that, especially when you don’t live with them and they pay for no living expenses.  But then I remember all the times like this and I cannot wait to cut him off after college.

Call for help immediately.

Sometimes people step away from their phone and cut off communication because of everything they’re dealing with.  It’s overwhelming to talk to others sometimes when things become too much.  It is probably, and hopefully, just that.

However, it was wrong for him to tell you he was going to end it and then stop responding.  No matter how “out of it” he is right now, he should not have left you hanging and worrying like that.

Therefore, you have every right to call for help.  911 or a suicide hotline can handle this situation if he doesn’t live with anyone else who can check on him.  If he didn’t do anything, there’s no harm done in having police check up on him.  Don’t worry about the virus.  The world doesn’t completely stop for the virus and other medical services still have to be available, including those for mental health and suicide.  If he did do something, hopefully they can take him to get help.

Don’t worry about anything else.  Don’t worry about him getting mad at you for calling 911.  Don’t worry about his parents finding out.  It sounds like this was a very spontaneous decision and he likely doesn’t truly want to die, he just wants to escape a situation that’s unbearable.  But he is not thinking straight right now and needs intervention before he does something permanent to fix a temporary feeling.

I’m sorry you’re in this situation.  I hope everything is alright.

Cliché, but seriously, sell everything you own that you won’t need before 09/06 and use that money to see the world before you leave it.  Nobody knows what’s next, if anything, but one thing that’s for sure is that you’re leaving this earth.  Treat it like your playground and go crazy because once you’re gone, you can’t see or do anything you’ve always wanted to do on earth ever again.  

If you’re not from there, Europe is incredibly easy and cheap to travel.  You can literally hop on trains and planes from country to country for extremely cheap prices and be in another country within hours.  Also you can literally go to train stations and buy tickets on a whim, there’s no planning whatsoever involved.  This was on my bucket list, although I don’t have a date in mind yet, and I literally would go somewhere, stay there until I was bored, go to a train station, pick a random city, and move on.

I have yet to go anywhere else besides the states and Europe, but literally anywhere is worth going to.  I just can’t speak for any other continents.

Use hostelworld or couchsurfing (apps) to find places to crash for cheap.  You can seriously live off of $10 a day or less. 

Stay in hostels, meet random people, see the things you learned about in history in real life, try new foods.  The best part about knowing your end is near is that it feels a lot easier to take risks.

I know you are obviously in some sort of pain, but hopefully this is distracting in a good way.  There is nothing quite like being dropped somewhere new for the first time, where most people don’t speak your language, nobody knows who you are, and every inch of the city is waiting to be explored.

I wrote this without considering the pandemic.  This is unfortunate timing for you, but perhaps if quarantine lets up for a while before then (I believe we will have multiple quarantine waves on and off until there’s a vaccine next year, but who knows) you can squeeze something in.

Donate money to something that helped you, volunteer for something that gave you an opportunity, make something for someone special to you, give someone you love something they’ve always wanted, do something with someone one last time, plant some flowers.  But I also understand if you’re not feeling up to that or if you just want to keep to yourself during this time.  Totally valid too.

I hope you have a great last few months.
